title: Image Western Blots for quantitative immunoblotting using the Bio-Rad VersaDoc CCD camera
author: Doug Campbell

steps_raw.instruction: SOP #13 Imaging Western Blots *IMPORTANT: Do NOT scratch glass inside Versadoc. No metal tools should be used around plates. 1. Turn on Black Box on benchtop (Turns on camera). You should hear a faint click. 2. Turn on Versadoc (It will go through its self-test. Lights on the door will cycle/flash). 3. Start computer program called Quantity One 4. Select File, & under tabs select Versadoc. The computer will then connect to Versadoc and camera 5. A Select Application screen should then pop up, press the select button and under Blotting select chemic super sensitivity . 6. Select Highlight Saturation. This will ensure if you have over-exposed the camera, the pixels will turn red. Red pixels can no longer be quantified. 7. Focus the camera :1st red sticker on the far left is for top plate for small western blot, 2nd red sticker is for bottom plate focus. Make sure you use 1.4 for the aperture size of the camera. It is the largest opening size, and will ensure all the light from your horse-radish peroxidase reaction will be recognized by the camera. 8. Wet the plate with some H2O and place transparency containing PVDF & detection reagents on the top plate. (see instructions for preparing detection reagents below) 9. Place the membrane on the transparency, and hit Preview button for 1 second. 10. Press Optimal Exposure (stacking) button. Set exposure times (between 10/30 seconds for starting image, between 60/300 seconds for end time....determined experimentally). Press OK and the machine will begin the imaging process. WRITE DOWN exposure times in your book so you will remember and help guide future researchers. Exposure times can also be determined by getting image “info” either in VersaDoc or Image Lab software. Side Note: If the Versadoc gives you an error, press OK and select Optimal Exposure again. Re-enter the exposure times and the machine should now begin working properly. 11. Take the best 2-3 photos out of the 30 you have taken. Note: Any red areas in the photos are indicators that the area has surpassed the machines quantitation capability of the CCD (Charge Capture Device which has a limit of 56,165 photons) and the data can no longer be quantified as the area is super saturated. 12. Select an Image you think looks decent and select Image then Transform a new window should pop-up and use the Gamma Function to make your selected image look nicer. 13. Save the nice image as both a jpeg and a SCN file and put a copy on C drive, M drive and DROP BOX. Use the year.month.day format to save the image. 14. Press print to print a copy of the image for your notebook. Press page setup in print screen to set paper size to 1280 by 1280. 15. Take Transparency out of Versadoc. Remove any excess liquid on the transparency into the green bin. 16. Use Tweezers and place PVDF back into the container with the block. Natalie Donaher September 2017 Page 1 of 2

A new window should pop-up and use the Gamma Function to make your selected image look nicer. 14. Save the nice image as both a jpeg and a SCN file and put a copy on C drive, M drive and DROP BOX. Use the year.month.day format to save the image. 15. Press print to print a copy of the image for your notebook. Press page setup in print screen to set paper size to 1280 by 1280. 16. Take Transparency out of Versadoc. Remove any excess liquid on the transparency into the green bin. 17. Use Tweezers and place PVDF back into the container with the block. 18. Wipe down the wet plate with kimwipe. 19. When finished with the Versadoc turn it off along with the camera, and the computer. Side note: The lower shelf can be used for UV illumination (agarose gels) and trans-illumination (blue-stained protein gels) while the top shelf is used for auto-illumination like that in Western Blotting. How to prepare PVDF for Imaging: 1. Take container containing the PVDF (membrane) and the block and bring it into Versadoc Room. Also bring tweezers and transparencies. 2. Use tweezers to remove the PVDF from block and transfers it onto a transparency. 3. Combine 1:1 Luminol and peroxide to form 850uL of ECL reagent (per sheet of PVDF). 4. Wet the PVDF using the ECL reagent ensuring area where bands will appear is completely covered in reagent. 5. Place the transparency containing the PVDF on the wet plate inside the Versadoc.
